title: Honey-Garlic Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
subtitle: sprouts roasted until crisp and caramelized with bits of bacon, then tossed in a honey-garlic glaze
imageAlt: Glossy roasted halved Brussels sprouts with crisp bacon pieces in a white dish on a navy napkin
servingsNote: a side for two, with leftovers for lunch

beforeYouStart.text: Oven at 220°C (425°F). A hot oven is what makes sprouts sweet instead of bitter.
Choose small, tight, bright green sprouts. Halve big ones through the stem so the leaves hold together.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Toss the sprouts with the oil, salt and pepper on the sheet and turn them cut side down. Scatter the bacon pieces between them.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Roast 20 minutes, until the cut sides are deep golden and the bacon is crisp.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Stir the honey, garlic and vinegar together, drizzle over the sprouts and toss on the sheet. Roast 3–4 minutes more, until sticky.

fixIt.fix: They were steamed, not roasted. Don't crowd the sheet, and roast until the cut sides are really brown.
The sprouts were too big. Quarter large ones and keep them about the same size.
Pieces were too close together. Spread them out, or give the sheet 3–5 minutes more before glazing.
Honey burns fast at 220°C. Keep the last roast to 3–4 minutes.

saleTip: Brussels sprouts are cheapest and best from October to January. Look for loose sprouts or 680 g bags on sale at No Frills.
swap: Green beans: same method, 12–15 minutes before glazing.
leftovers: Chop and fold into fried rice or a frittata, or reheat in a hot skillet until crisp again.
doneness: Cut sides deep golden, centres tender when pierced with a knife, bacon crisp.
source: Based on tested roasted Brussels sprout methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): roasted cut side down at 220°C (425°F), glazed at the end.
prepAhead: Trim and halve the sprouts up to 2 days ahead and keep them in a bag in the fridge.
reheat: In a hot skillet 3–4 minutes, or at 200°C (400°F) 5–8 minutes, until hot and crisp again.

basic.note: Simply roasted with a honey drizzle, no bacon.

stepNotes.3: Basic: drizzle with just the honey.

fancy.note: Dried cranberries and a shower of Parmesan to finish.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: toss in the cranberries with the glaze.

addSteps.title: Fancy finish
addSteps.text: Pile into a warm dish and scatter the Parmesan over the top.

plating: Cut sides up so the caramelized faces show.
Parmesan over the top at the last second.
A shallow white dish keeps them from steaming.

why.0-0: Cut side down on a hot sheet gives the deep browning that makes sprouts sweet.
why.1-2: A teaspoon of vinegar balances the honey so the glaze isn't cloying.

funFact: Brussels sprouts taste milder than they used to: Dutch plant breeders in the 1990s bred out much of the bitter compound, which is why many people who hated them as kids like them now.
pairs: a green side for Christmas dinner
